subject: Renewal coordination: EU jurisdictional node + APAC satellite capacity
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Natalie King <natalie.king@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal coordination: EU jurisdictional node + APAC satellite capacity

Hi Natalie,

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last week. Per our follow-up, I wanted to put a concise proposal on the table so procurement and engineering on your side have something concrete to react to. High level: Crestline is renewing for another 12 months and wants two changes in the term-of-service and capacity model:

- EU jurisdictional node (data residency): provision a dedicated EU node (Frankfurt) that ensures PHI/PII processing and persistent storage remain in the EU. We will surface a DPA amendment and allow KMS integration (customer-managed keys preferred).
- APAC satellite: a warm standby in APAC (Singapore) for burst capacity and cross-region failover with prefix/KV cache seeding for faster cold-starts. This is primarily for latency improvement for APAC users and to support failover during EU maintenance windows.

Proposed commercial impact (draft): committed tokens/month increase from 2M -> 5M; committed price uplift ~+18% on monthly committed; one-time migration/validation fee (engineering runbook + legal changes) $7,500. Exact numbers in attached SOW draft.

What we need from you to move forward:
- Confirm whether Crestline requires customer-hosted KMS (we can support both) and whether logs/audit exports must remain in-EU as well.
- PO or procurement timeline and legal contact for the DPA amendment.
- Any technical constraints for failover (e.g., maximum allowed cross-region replication latency, required RTO/RPO thresholds).

I've attached the draft SOW, an architecture sketch for the EU node, and a DPA template for legal to review. Suggest a 30-minute kickoff next week to align stakeholders and get a firm timeline for a July Q3 rollout.

If you prefer, we can tighten the SOW and issue a DocuSign amendment once we have procurement details.

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Renewals, EMEA
Redwood Inference
-- attachments: redwood_sow_draft_v1.pdf, eu-node-arch.png, dpa-template.docx

From: Natalie King <natalie.king@crestlinehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Crestline Procurement <procurement@crestlinehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T13:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal coordination: EU jurisdictional node + APAC satellite capacity

Hi Hannah,

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifying questions from our side before we lock dates:

1) KMS: Our security team strongly prefers customer-managed keys residing in an EU KMS (Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS EU-only). Can you confirm the steps for key rotation and backup for that setup?
2) What exactly is covered by "data stays in EU" — are logs, aggregated metrics, and trace spans also considered residency-sensitive? We will need a definitive list to present to legal.
3) Pricing: can you provide a not-to-exceed cadence (monthly cap) so the board can sign off?
4) SLA and failover: what's the expected RTO/RPO for the APAC satellite failover? We need numbers to feed into our incident response plan.

I've attached our internal requirements spreadsheet showing peak hours, latency SLAs by region, and a short note from our security lead. If we can get the answers above, procurement will start prepping an internal PO and I'll loop in our legal lead (cc'd in a later thread).

Proposing a meeting on 2027-06-02; we prefer late morning CEST.

Best,
Natalie

--
Natalie King
Head of Engineering Operations
Crestline Health Systems
-- attachments: crestline_requirements_20270528.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Natalie King <natalie.king@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T07:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal coordination: EU jurisdictional node + APAC satellite capacity

Natalie / team,

Quick technical write-up to answer the specific questions so legal/procurement/security have something concrete:

- KMS and keys: We fully support customer-managed keys in EU KMS (we've onboarded multiple customers to AWS KMS EU/Frankfurt and Azure Key Vault EU). Key material never leaves the EU when you opt for customer-managed keys; Redwood stores only key identifiers and performs crypto ops via the EU KMS endpoint. Rotation and backup are handled via the customer's KMS policies; we recommend a quarterly rotation cadence documented in the SOW.

- What "stays in EU": Persistent storage (model KV caches persisted to disk), request/response payloads, audit logs, and user-created artifacts will remain on the EU node. Aggregated telemetry (non-identifiable metrics) can be routed to our central analytics; if you require that telemetry remain in region, we will route it to an EU analytics sink. Trace spans and debug logs that contain identifiers are configurable to be scrubbed or kept in-region. We'll add a section to the DPA that enumerates the exact data categories.

- APAC satellite failover behavior:
  - Deploy a warm standby in APAC (Singapore) with prefix/KV cache seeding from recent EU traffic.
  - Failover policy: automated tiered failover (region health + control-plane decisioning) with manual approval window for major changes.
  - RTO target: 5–15 minutes for traffic redirection; RPO: up to 10 minutes for non-persistent cache-backed flows. For persistent writes we will ensure commit to EU primary before marking success unless you opt-in to asynchronous replication (we don't recommend for PHI).

- Commercial / caps: The +18% committed monthly uplift is our standard for the additional dedicated-residency and reserved-node guarantee; we can add a monthly not-to-exceed cap in the amendment — propose a 10% buffer over committed tokens as a reasonable cap before we enter overage billing. One-time engineering validation fee $7,500 covers migration testing and compliance artifacts requested by your security team.

I've created a Jira ticket for the infra work: INFRA-4579 (link below). Attaching a short config snippet for the EU node for your security engineers to review.

Let us know if you want the EU telemetry to stay fully within-region; that is an option but will add modest onboarding time (2–3 extra working days).

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal coordination: EU jurisdictional node + APAC satellite capacity

Thanks everyone — great alignment. Next steps proposed below so we have clear owners/timeline: 

1) Hannah / Crestline procurement: Crestline to share PO or procurement timeframe; legal contact for the DPA. Target: PO in hand by 2027-06-10.
2) Karthik / Infra: Reserve EU node in Frankfurt and spin up APAC standby (provisioning target the week of 2027-07-11). Owner: Karthik.
3) Security / Legal: We'll update DPA and enumerate logs/telemetry categories; Karthik to provide the EU-only telemetry option brief. Owner: Hannah / Karthik.
4) Commercial: Draft amendment with a not-to-exceed monthly cap (10% buffer) and one-time migration fee included. Ben to circulate final numbers and DocuSign link for signature.

Proposed meeting: 2027-06-02 10:00 CEST — 30 min. I'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda (attached). If that works, please accept and loop in your legal/procurement lead.

Once the amendment is signed we'll schedule the staging failover demo and a runbook review; that demo is useful for your SREs to validate RTO/RPO.

Best,
Hannah

--

Head of Renewals, EMEA
Redwood Inference
